PokéChamp is designed as a competitive language agent that achieves expert-level performance in two-player turn-based Pokémon battles. Its architecture integrates a large language model (LLM) into a minimax tree search algorithm. Specifically, the LLM replaces three core modules within this search: player action sampling, opponent modeling, and state value function estimation. This allows PokéChamp to leverage gameplay history and human knowledge to refine its search space and manage partial observability in the game.

Information regarding the architecture of 'PokeHit' or the responsibilities of an LLM within such a bot is not available.
